Q5.title: Q5: Operating Margin and Cumulative Return Across Sectors
Q5.solution: Aggregate firm/sector observations to compute mean operating margin, first-to-last operating margin change, and compounded cumulative return prod(1 + r_t) - 1. Evaluate cross-sector correlation, average within-sector firm correlation, 95% confidence intervals, and compare cumulative returns across margin regimes (rising vs. high-initial vs. other).
Q5.summary: Summary (Q5): Sectors with persistently high or improving operating margins typically exhibit stronger compounding and lower operational fragility, though cross-sectional correlation depends on valuation multiples and cyclicality.

Q6.title: Q6: Event Study [-10, +10] Around Earnings Announcements
Q6.solution: Align daily returns relative to each firm's earnings announcement date (t = 0) across the [-10, +10] trading-day window. Compute mean daily return, cumulative return trajectory, event counts, and 95% confidence intervals at each lag/lead t to test for pre-announcement drift, immediate reaction, and post-earnings drift.
Q6.summary: Summary (Q6): Examining t in [-10, +10] isolates information arrival around earnings disclosures, distinguishing price discovery at t=0 from pre-event anticipation and post-announcement drift.

Q7.title: Q7: Forecast Error and Estimate Revisions by Sector
Q7.solution: Compute forecast error (Actual - Estimate, or direct error column) and sequential estimate revisions delta Estimate_t by sector. Summarize sample count, mean error (optimism/pessimism bias), mean absolute error |Error|, dispersion (std), and share of positive surprises.
Q7.summary: Summary (Q7): Mean absolute forecast error and revision volatility capture earnings predictability across sectors, highlighting where consensus expectations lag fundamentals or macro shifts.

Q8.title: Q8: Debt Ratio vs. Return Volatility and Sharp-Drop Regimes
Q8.solution: Measure sector mean leverage (debt ratio) and return standard deviation overall and separately during sharp-drop days (returns in the bottom 10% tail) versus ordinary days. Compute cross-sector correlation between leverage and volatility.
Q8.summary: Summary (Q8): Financial leverage amplifies equity risk during market stress; comparing ordinary vs. bottom-decile sharp-drop volatility shows whether high-debt sectors experience disproportionate tail amplification.

Q9.title: Q9: Fate of Low-PBR (PBR < 1) Companies
Q9.solution: Filter observations with PBR < 1 to identify sector concentration, split returns by profitability (ROE >= 0 vs. ROE < 0), and track whether firms with PBR < 1 eventually recover to PBR >= 1 or remain below 1 by the end of the sample.
Q9.summary: Summary (Q9): Low-PBR stocks split into value traps (persistent low PBR and weak/negative ROE) and turnaround/re-rating candidates (positive ROE or recovery to PBR >= 1).
